width_is_self_identifying.finding: Every decode step in the capture carries EXACTLY 96*width GDN launches (48 layers x {L0,L1} x width). Measured histogram: 96->4 steps, 192->74, 288->237, 384->225. The reducer raises if any step's count is not a multiple of 96.
width_is_self_identifying.consequence: Binning by width needs no census join; the launch count IS the width. Cross-checked against the census batch_size histogram {1:4, 2:74, 3:236, 4:225}.

does_the_56_1_pct_handoff_share_hold_at_.answer: YES -- it is width-invariant to within 0.04 percentage points. But the 56.1% figure itself is the probe's inflated rendering.
does_the_56_1_pct_handoff_share_hold_at_.denominator_defect_in_the_published_figu: cost_probe.json computed handoff_fraction = 128.256 / two_launch_total(228.736) = 0.5607. The 128.256 numerator is assembled from ISOLATED ablations (L0_deployed - L0_no_export = 45.984; L1_len1 = 82.272) whose parent launches sum to 249.920 in isolation, not to the 228.736 back-to-back pair. Against a consistent denominator the B1 handoff fraction is 128.256/249.920 = 0.5132.
does_the_56_1_pct_handoff_share_hold_at_.width_transfer_method: The handoff lives inside each launch at shares alpha = export_write/L0 = 0.50192 and beta = (parent_read+1 step)/L1 = 0.51971. In-situ handoff fraction at width w = alpha*s0(w) + beta*s1(w) with s0,s1 the measured L0/L1 time shares of the pair.
does_the_56_1_pct_handoff_share_hold_at_.why_it_is_flat: The mix DOES shift -- L1's share of the pair rises from 67.64% at width 1 to 69.47% at width 4 (L0 -4.7% per launch, L1 +3.8% per launch). It moves the handoff fraction by +0.033 pp only because L0 and L1 happen to carry nearly identical handoff shares (0.502 vs 0.520). The invariance is arithmetic luck, not a deep law -- but it is measured, not assumed.

the_load_bearing_structural_measurement.finding: The gridZ sequence within every step is strictly alternating 0,1,0,1,... and the measured L0->L1 gap is median -0.13 us (adjacent, zero intervening kernels on the stream) at EVERY width. Zero kernels of any name execute between an export write and its parent read.
the_load_bearing_structural_measurement.consequence: The handoff's L2 regime is identical at width 1 and width 4: only ONE request's 3 MiB state tile is ever live in the 24 MiB L2 at a time; co-resident requests never evict each other's handoff. This is why per-launch cost is width-invariant (width-4 pair / width-1 pair = 1.0105) and why the B1 ratio transfers.
the_load_bearing_structural_measurement.corroborates: results/fr13_b4_padded_b4_derisk_20260813 section 4 -- GDN is 2-12 CTA/SM, LINEAR in CTAs (R^2=.996), no wave staircase. Measured here end-to-end: the lever is handoff-BYTES-based at width 4 exactly as at B1.

overlap_check.finding: Union vs plain sum of GDN kernel intervals differs by 0.09-0.12% at every width (single stream, serialized).
overlap_check.consequence: Kernel time removed IS wall removed. The reducer raises above 1% overlap.

width_4_price.which_model_is_right: The floor applies the probe's ABSOLUTE per-pair saving (40.096 us) unchanged. The central applies the probe's RATIO (0.17529) to the measured in-situ pair cost (260.64 us). They differ because the trace's pair costs 13.9% more than the probe's back-to-back two_launch_total. That gap is NOT mostly CUPTI: the trace's width-1 pair (257.92 us) sits only +3.2% above the probe's ISOLATED L0+L1 sum (249.92 us) while sitting +12.8% above its L2-warm fused pair (228.74 us). Reading: the probe's 21.2 us of L0->L1 L2-reuse benefit is largely NOT realised in production, because the layer's own 48 MiB export/parent working set overflows a 24 MiB L2 regardless of adjacency. The handoff is therefore MORE DRAM-resident in production than in the probe -- which is exactly the probe's self-declared understatement, now quantified. The ratio model is the honest central; the floor is genuinely a floor.
width_4_price.upper_bound_caveat: The 13.8 ms upper assumes single_launch itself is completely insensitive to the production memory environment. It still reads q/k/v/g/beta and writes out + 4 rings, so that is too strong. Reported as unpriced upside, not carried.

width_3_price.note: Width 3 is the MODAL width of the operating point.
width_3_price.as_built_reason: fixed32_batch_gdn_selector returns None for batch 3 (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:3512-3514) and the descriptor guard raises unless batch == 4 (:17143). The route does not run at width 3 at all.

window_level_value.reading: As built the lever is worth 0.55% of window wall -- about 29% of what the sealed FA2 gqa_pair lever realised. Widening to b2/b3 roughly doubles it to 1.08%, still just over half the FA2 lever. Licensed by gaps.json: the GPU is ~95% busy and effectively serial in this window (plain kernel sum / window = 0.949), so kernel time removed is window wall removed.

out_of_step_headroom_is_structurally_unr.method: 32,304 out-of-step launches (99.6% eager, not graph-captured) cluster into 6,936 bursts separated by >2 ms. Burst sizes are exactly 2, 4 and 6 launches = 1, 2 and 3 co-resident requests. 6936/48 layers = 144.5, matching the 144 mixed passes in results/fr13_b4_prefill_gaps_20260813.
out_of_step_headroom_is_structurally_unr.finding: NO mixed pass ever runs GDN at batch 4. A batch==4-only route can never reach this 4.28 s.

is_the_kernel_body_b_agnostic.answer: It is batch-INDEXED, not batch-agnostic -- and that is the stronger position.
is_the_kernel_body_b_agnostic.mechanism: pid_batch = tl.program_id(2) (:10720-10722); every surface (q,k,v,beta,g,raw_a,raw_b,out,ring_k,ring_v,ring_a,ring_b,ring_k_norm,ring_gate) addressed through global_node = pid_batch * N_ACTUAL + node_c (:10527); h0 bank indexing batch-aware at :10741/:10748 via H0_ACCEPTED_BATCH_STRIDE and H0_INDEX_BATCH_STRIDE.
is_the_kernel_body_b_agnostic.tier_a_argument: There is no cross-batch reduction anywhere in the body: each pid_batch slice reads and writes only its own N_ACTUAL rows. Accumulation order within a slice is identical to the b=1 case. Byte invariance in b therefore holds BY CONSTRUCTION, not by the restriction argument the FA2 unit needed. The residual risk is codegen only (Triton may schedule differently at gridZ=4), which is precisely why this is a gate and not an assert -- the same disposition the B1 seal took, where the codegen risk did not materialise.
is_the_kernel_body_b_agnostic.static_asserts: None. This is Triton/Python; every check is a Python raise. The padded-B4 lesson ('check every static_assert and hardcoded batch') resolves here to the two batch literals in part_2.what_is_missing.3 plus the two verified-consistent surfaces below.

invocation_counter.concern: The single_launch kernel's counter guard (:10723-10729) is mask=(pid_vh==0)&(pid_v==0) with NO pid_batch term, unlike the sibling path kernel (:10309-10315) which carries &(pid_path==0). At gridZ=batch this yields `batch` increments, not 1.
invocation_counter.resolution: NOT A DEFECT -- it is what makes the surfaces agree. The gate's reference at b=4 is _launch_reference (:17509), which loops `for request in range(batch)` calling the SERVED per-request launch_tree_gdn_prepared, each contributing 1 increment (COUNT_INVOCATION gated to level 0 at :16395) = `batch` increments total. Candidate `batch`, reference `batch`. They match at b=4 and at b=1.
invocation_counter.verified_by: source read at both call sites; not yet by hardware.

flags.concern: flags are written only by pid_batch==0 (:10872-10874) while the wrapper enforces flags_rows == batch (:17214).
flags.resolution: CONSISTENT. Both arms store flags[0]=1 and flags[1]=FLAGS_ROWS; the reference loop passes the SAME staging_rows=flags_rows to every per-request call (:17551-17552), so both write the literal 4. The per-request writes are idempotent to identical bytes.

physical_grid_z.finding: The static descriptor is pinned to (1,) and validated as (1,) by BOTH launch paths (:16112 B1, :17149 B4), while the EXECUTED record reports (batch,) (:17425-17431). This split is intentional -- the descriptor describes one batch element's shape -- and is test-pinned (tests/test_fr13_fixed32_gdn_single_launch_ordered.py:121 and :261).
physical_grid_z.consequence: No change needed for b=4. It IS the b1-shaped literal one would otherwise trip over.

gate_reference_is_the_served_route.finding: The b4 gate does not compare the folded kernel against a batched two-launch stand-in. _launch_reference (:17509) drives the real served per-request launch_tree_gdn_prepared once per request over slices q[start:end] etc., sharing the SAME out/ring/flags/counter buffers the candidate writes.
gate_reference_is_the_served_route.consequence: A b4 PASS proves single_launch == the route actually in the nsys trace, with no intermediate reference needing its own qualification. This closes the gate-scope question before it is asked.

no_regression_risk_at_untreated_widths.finding: Arming _FR13_FIXED32_GDN_SINGLE_LAUNCH changes dispatch ONLY at batch 4; widths 1-3 fall through to the identical unchanged per-request route in both arms.
no_regression_risk_at_untreated_widths.consequence: The NATURAL PLACEBO the padded-B4 FA2 design had to be engineered for is here for free: widths 1,2,3 are byte-identical stock code on both sides of a timing pair, so the per-width strata + DiD instrument (scripts/fr13_b4_gqa_width4_pair_reduce.py, results/fr13_b4_width4_nsys_20260813) applies directly with no new measurement design.

power_analysis.note: The FA2 seal measured mean 27.03, SD 13.77 at n=4 (raw per-pass 7.54/39.62/32.33/28.6). If that SD is ADDITIVE in wall it exceeds this entire effect and n=4 cannot seal. If the CV (0.509) is the invariant -- which is what 'variance = per-pass trajectory composition' implies, since composition scales the effect multiplicatively -- then n=4 seals comfortably. THIS IS THE PRINCIPAL MEASUREMENT RISK ON THE LEVER.

build_because: The route is already built end-to-end and green offline (54 tests). Phases 0-1 are 'run what exists', not 'write a route'.

The Tier-A legality argument is structural and strong: explicit per-batch-element indexing with no cross-batch reduction, gate reference = the actual served per-request route sharing the same buffers, counter and flags semantics verified consistent at b=4 from source.
The saving clears the 4.20 ms MDE at 1.83x (floor) to 2.09x (central) at width 4.

The handoff share is MEASURED width-invariant (51.40% -> 51.43%), and the mechanism is measured not assumed: zero-gap L0->L1 adjacency at every width means the L2 handoff regime at width 4 is the B1 regime.
The natural placebo is free -- widths 1-3 are identical stock code in both arms -- so the padded-B4 measurement instrument applies with no new design.
The probe understates: production's handoff is more DRAM-resident than the L2-warm probe (trace width-1 pair sits +12.8% above the probe's fused pair), so the floor is a genuine floor.
caveats: It is a 2.1% lever. As built it reaches only the 225/540 width-4 steps = 0.55% of window wall, roughly 29% of what the sealed FA2 gqa_pair lever realised.
WIDTH 3 -- the modal width, 43.9% of steps -- pays EXACTLY ZERO as built. The single largest scoping fact in this document.
The 4.28 s out-of-step GDN is measurably unreachable: mixed passes run GDN at 1, 2 or 3 requests and NEVER at 4.
Productionisation is genuinely missing (no production credential validator) and, on FA2 precedent, will surface boot-class defects.
Sealing power is the principal risk: if pass-to-pass SD is additive in wall (13.77 ms as observed for FA2) it exceeds the whole effect and needs ~9 passes.
The width transfer is argued from trace-measured per-launch costs, not measured at b=4 geometry. Phase 0 retires this caveat for ~0.4 GPU-h.
part_5_verdict.recommended_sequence: Phase 0 (b=4 probe) -> Phase 1 (existing b4 gate) -> Phase 2 (productionisation + re-gate) -> Phase 3 (n=1 screen, settles the variance model) -> then take the Phase 4 budget decision to Mark with a measured effect and a measured SD in hand.

does_not_claim: No acceptance, regression or step-envelope reading. The capture is CUPTI-attached for its whole lifetime; every absolute time here is profiler-perturbed and is reported, never subtracted.

The 7.7-8.8 ms/step width-4 figure is a PRICED EXPECTATION from a synthetic B1 kernel probe transferred through trace-measured per-launch costs. It is not a measured step-wall delta and must not be quoted as one.

No claim that single_launch is byte-identical at b=4. The B1 seal (427d8cba..., hydra27:b1) licenses b=1 only. The b=4 counter and flags agreement is verified from source at both call sites and has never executed on hardware.
The width-3 'if extended' prices assume the b2/b3 widening behaves like b4. That widening is unbuilt and ungated.
The out-of-step burst-width finding characterises THIS 360 s prefill-heavy window; the analysis.md honesty note (window overstates prefill share by ~8 pp vs the 4,431 s arm) applies unchanged.
The 0.509 CV variance model is an inference from the FA2 seal's decomposition, not a measurement of this lever's variance.
